departments.name: Economy and Simulation
departments.mission: Make value circulate: supply and demand, currency, production chains, markets, scarcity and believable economic actors.

deliverables.name: Economy Model
acceptance: Every good and currency listed with source, sink and base value
Price formation and update cadence specified
Production chain graph included with conversion rates
Failure states (hyperinflation, dead markets) stated with guards

deliverables.name: Economy Implementation
acceptance: Prices respond to supply and demand as modelled
Transactions are atomic and cannot duplicate value
Economy state persists through save and load

deliverables.name: Economy Soak and Exploit Review
acceptance: Long-run simulation shows no runaway inflation or currency collapse
Known money-duplication paths tested and closed
Price and volume time series attached as evidence

gates: An economy with no sink or no failure guard is rejected
Any duplication exploit found in testing is a release blocker

departments.name: Population and Society Simulation
departments.mission: Populate the world with people who have identity, routine and relationships, and let their society evolve plausibly.

deliverables.name: Population and Society Design
acceptance: NPC archetypes listed with roles, schedules and needs
Relationship and faction model defined
Population caps and simulation LOD stated in numbers
Identity generation rules stated so no two NPCs are identical

deliverables.name: Population Simulation
acceptance: NPCs follow schedules and change jobs and relationships over time
Population simulation runs within its per-tick budget at cap
Simulation state persists through save and load

deliverables.name: Society Simulation Review
acceptance: Long-run simulation does not collapse, stall or produce immortal NPCs
Off-screen simulation LOD verified as behaviour-preserving
Measured tick cost at maximum population attached

gates: A population system with no cap or LOD is rejected
NPCs without identity or role variation are rejected

departments.name: Dynamic World Systems
departments.mission: Keep the world moving: day and night, weather, seasons, disasters, environmental change and persistent destruction.
capabilities: seasonal change and its gameplay effects

deliverables.name: Dynamic World Design
acceptance: Cycle lengths, weather probabilities and season effects stated numerically
Each dynamic system listed with its gameplay consequences
Persistence rules for destruction and change defined
Performance scaling rules stated per quality tier

deliverables.name: Dynamic World Implementation
acceptance: Time, weather and seasons advance and are observable in a build
Effects on gameplay systems are applied through one authoritative clock
World state persists through save and load

deliverables.name: Dynamic World Review
acceptance: Worst-case weather and disaster scenarios measured within frame budget
No state desync between visuals, simulation and saved data
Lowest quality tier verified with all systems active

gates: A dynamic system with no persisted state is rejected
Unbounded weather VFX cost is rejected
